title: Kelowna Inaugural Council Meeting & Swearing-In (2026–2030)
location: Mary Irwin Theatre, Rotary Centre for the Arts, 421 Cawston Ave, Kelowna, BC
desc: Judge Clarke Burnett administers the Oath of Office to Mayor Tom Dyas and Councillors Les Bellamy, Kevin Kraft, Davis Kyle, Gord Lovegrove, Brady Rogers, Mohini Singh, Laura Thurnheer and Rick Webber. One-hour ceremony followed by a public coffee and appetizer reception until 9 p.m. Open to the public; livestreamed at kelowna.ca/council. Good networking opportunity with the new council.
gr_note: The first chance to meet the full 2026–2030 Kelowna council in an informal setting; the reception is ideal for introducing yourself to new councillors before their portfolios and committee roles are set.
attendees: Mayor Tom Dyas and all eight councillors, Judge Clarke Burnett, City senior staff, families, community and business leaders
access: Open to the public; reception with coffee and appetizers follows the ceremony until 9 p.m.

title: West Kelowna Inaugural Council Meeting + First Regular Meeting
location: West Kelowna City Hall Council Chambers, 3731 Old Okanagan Hwy, West Kelowna, BC
desc: Acclaimed Mayor Stephen Johnston and Councillors Justin Chapman, Tasha Da Silva, Rick de Jong, Tom Groat, Garrett Millsap and Chris Moyer are sworn in, followed by the first regular council meeting. Expect appointments to the RDCO board. Public welcome; webcast at westkelownacity.ca/webcasts. In Dan Albas's riding.
gr_note: Sets the term's tone in Dan Albas's riding; watch for RDCO board appointments and deputy-mayor rotation, which decide who represents West Kelowna regionally.
attendees: Mayor Stephen Johnston and Councillors Justin Chapman, Tasha Da Silva, Rick de Jong, Tom Groat, Garrett Millsap and Chris Moyer; City staff

title: Peachland Inaugural Council Meeting & Swearing-In
location: Peachland Council Chambers, Peachland Community Centre, 4450 6th Street, Peachland, BC
desc: Corporate Officer Jennifer Sawatzky administers the oath to Mayor-elect Gail Mansell and six councillors-elect. Peachland is in Dan Albas's riding. Venue is where Peachland council normally meets; confirm on peachland.ca.
gr_note: Peachland's new council will decide its RDCO director and committee appointments here.
attendees: Mayor-elect Gail Mansell, six councillors-elect, Corporate Officer Jennifer Sawatzky
unconfirmed: Venue assumed to be the usual council chambers; confirm on peachland.ca.

title: West Kelowna Agricultural Advisory Committee
location: West Kelowna City Hall Council Chambers, 3731 Old Okanagan Hwy, West Kelowna, BC
desc: Monthly meeting (first Wednesday) of the City of West Kelowna Agricultural Advisory Committee. Open to the public.
gr_note: Where ALR and farm-related land-use applications are vetted before council.
attendees: Committee members (local farmers and residents), council liaison, planning staff
agenda: Posted on westkelownacity.ca before the meeting

title: Accelerate Okanagan OFFSITE (founders & C-suite)
location: KF Centre for Excellence, Kelowna, BC
desc: Accelerate Okanagan's all-day event for founders and C-suite leaders, presented by TELUS: keynotes, panels, workshops and a closing networking happy hour. Exact hours weren't published; check Accelerate Okanagan.
gr_note: Tech-sector leaders are key stakeholders on innovation, talent and immigration policy.
access: Ticketed; aimed at founders and C-suite

title: DEADLINE: Register for 'Trade Diversification' with Canada's Chief Trade Commissioner
location: Online
desc: Registration deadline for the Nov 10 event in Kelowna. The Trade Commissioner Service lists Nov 5; Tourism Kelowna's roundup says registration through the Kelowna Chamber closes Nov 3.
organizer: Kelowna Chamber of Commerce / Trade Commissioner Service

title: Indigenous Veterans Day (Westbank First Nation ceremony: date TBC)
location: WFN Cenotaph, 1900 Quail Lane, Westbank, BC
desc: National Indigenous Veterans Day. Westbank First Nation, which sits in the heart of the riding, holds a public ceremony at its cenotaph every year; in 2025 it was held the Friday before (Nov 7, 10:30 a.m.–noon, lunch to follow). Nov 8 2026 is a Sunday, so check wfn.ca for this year's date. Chief, council and local elected officials usually attend.
gr_note: Attending WFN ceremonies builds relationships with WFN leadership, a self-governing First Nation and a major economic player in the riding.
attendees: WFN Chief and Council, veterans, members, local elected officials
access: Open to the public; lunch served afterwards in past years
unconfirmed: 2026 date and time not yet published by WFN.

title: Kelowna City Council: First Regular Meeting of New Term
location: Council Chamber, Kelowna City Hall, 1435 Water Street, Kelowna, BC
desc: First regular meeting of the 2026–2030 council. Kelowna's regular public meetings are Mondays at 1:30 p.m.; council also meets Monday mornings at 9 a.m. for policy and in-camera business. Livestreamed at kelowna.ca/council. Check the agenda for the exact times.
gr_note: The first business meeting of the new council signals early priorities and which staff reports come forward first.
attendees: Mayor and council, City senior staff, delegations
unconfirmed: Exact afternoon start time; check the agenda.

title: Trade Diversification: Where Do We Stand? (Sara Wilshaw, Chief Trade Commissioner)
location: Kelowna Innovation Centre (Theatre), 460 Doyle Avenue, Kelowna, BC
desc: A three-hour in-person session led by Sara Wilshaw, Canada's Chief Trade Commissioner, with the Kelowna Chamber, on diversifying into EU and Indo-Pacific markets. Highly relevant to federal trade policy and government relations. Start time not published (time TBC). Registration has closed (Chamber deadline Nov 3); Chamber event page: https://secure.kelownachamber.org/events/TradeDiversification%20Where%20Do%20We%20Stand-7843/details
gr_note: Rare local access to one of Canada's most senior trade officials; directly relevant to federal trade policy and Canada–US trade.
organizer: Kelowna Chamber of Commerce with the Trade Commissioner Service (Global Affairs Canada)
attendees: Sara Wilshaw (Chief Trade Commissioner of Canada), exporters, Chamber members

title: Remembrance Day: Kelowna (Legion Branch #26)
location: City Park Cenotaph, 1600 Abbott St, Kelowna, BC
desc: The region's largest ceremony: a parade from Bernard Ave & Water St to the City Park cenotaph, organized by Royal Canadian Legion Kelowna Branch #26. Elected officials lay wreaths. Times are based on past years; confirm closer to the date.
gr_note: Nearly every local elected official attends and lays a wreath; a respectful occasion to be seen in the community.
attendees: Veterans, Canadian Armed Forces, RCMP, cadets, Mayor and council, MPs and MLAs laying wreaths, thousands of residents
access: Open to the public; arrive early, crowds are large

title: Remembrance Day: West Kelowna (Legion Branch #288)
location: Royal LePage Place, 2760 Cameron Rd, West Kelowna, BC
desc: Hosted by Royal Canadian Legion Westbank Branch #288. The 2026 listing says to be seated by 10:30 a.m.; the service starts at 10:45, with the moment of silence at 11 and the service ending around noon. In past years an honour parade stepped off around 10 a.m. (parade time not confirmed for 2026). The MP and local councils usually attend.
gr_note: The main Remembrance Day ceremony in Dan Albas's riding.
attendees: Veterans, MP Dan Albas (usually), West Kelowna council, WFN representatives, residents
access: Open to the public; be seated by 10:30 a.m.

title: Remembrance Day: Peachland (Legion Branch #69)
location: Cenotaph Park, Beach Ave & 2nd St, Peachland, BC
desc: Ceremony at Cenotaph Park with a reception afterwards at Legion Branch #69. Times are based on past years; confirm closer to the date.
attendees: Veterans, Peachland mayor and council, residents
access: Open to the public; reception at the Legion afterwards

title: Remembrance Day: Summerland
location: Memorial Park, Wharton Street, Summerland, BC
desc: Parade of Legion members, veterans and the Summerland Pipe Band leaves Wharton St at 10:30 a.m. and marches to the Memorial Park cenotaph; two minutes of silence at 11. The Legion (14205 Rosedale Ave) opens at noon. Times are based on past years.
attendees: Veterans, Legion members, Summerland Pipe Band, mayor and council, residents
access: Open to the public; Legion (14205 Rosedale Ave) opens at noon

title: 35th Innkeeper's Gala: 'A Diamond Affair' (Hotel Eldorado 100th)
location: Hotel Eldorado, 500 Cook Rd, Kelowna, BC
desc: Billed as Kelowna's top charitable event; more than 350 guests and usually sells out. Proceeds go to Okanagan College's Centre for Food, Wine and Tourism and Kelowna General Hospital (including JoeAnna's House). A VIP 'Elevated Prelude' runs before the gala. Business and civic leaders attend. Tickets on Eventbrite.
gr_note: One of Kelowna's highest-profile charity evenings; good for meeting donors and business leaders who sit on local boards.
attendees: 350+ guests: business owners, hospitality and civic leaders
access: Ticketed; usually sells out (listed as almost full)

title: Kelowna: First Public Hearing of New Council
location: Council Chamber, Kelowna City Hall, 1435 Water Street, Kelowna, BC
desc: The new council's first Tuesday public hearing and regular meeting on development and zoning applications. The City's council guide lists Tuesday hearings at 4 p.m.; confirm on the agenda at kelowna.ca/council.
gr_note: The clearest window into how the new council votes on housing and development; watch who speaks on behalf of the development industry.
attendees: Mayor and council, planning staff, applicants, developers, neighbours speaking for or against applications
access: Open to the public; members of the public may speak to items on the hearing agenda
unconfirmed: Start time (4 p.m. per City guide); confirm on the agenda.

title: West Kelowna Advisory Planning Commission
location: West Kelowna City Hall Council Chambers, 3731 Old Okanagan Hwy, West Kelowna, BC
desc: Monthly meeting (third Wednesday) of the APC, which reviews land-use and development applications before they go to council.
agenda: Posted on westkelownacity.ca before the meeting

title: Tree of Hope Festival
location: Landmark District, 1700 Dickson Ave, Kelowna, BC
desc: Community holiday kickoff and charity festival at the Landmark District. Start time is from Eventbrite; the end time is an estimate.

title: West Kelowna Accessibility & Inclusion Committee
location: West Kelowna City Hall, 3731 Old Okanagan Hwy, West Kelowna, BC
desc: Scheduled meeting of the City of West Kelowna Accessibility and Inclusion Committee. Time not listed; check the city's calendar.

title: RDCO Inaugural Regular Board Meeting (new board, chair election)
location: RDCO Woodhaven Boardroom, 1450 KLO Rd, Kelowna, BC
desc: First meeting of the new Regional District of Central Okanagan board after the election; the chair and vice-chair are elected. Directors come from Kelowna, West Kelowna, Peachland, Lake Country and the electoral areas, with Westbank First Nation as a non-voting member. Streamed at rdco.com/board.
gr_note: The chair and vice-chair elected here shape regional decisions on transit, parks, water and emergency management for the whole Central Okanagan.
attendees: Directors from Kelowna, West Kelowna, Peachland, Lake Country and the electoral areas; Westbank First Nation (non-voting); RDCO senior staff

title: Kelowna Chamber 39th Annual Business Excellence Awards Gala
location: Delta Hotels by Marriott Grand Okanagan Resort, 1310 Water Street, Kelowna, BC
desc: The Kelowna Chamber of Commerce's biggest night of the year, recognizing local businesses in its 120th anniversary year. Co-presented by Lawson Lundell LLP and BEEM Credit Union. Draws the Kelowna business community along with the mayor, councillors, MLAs and often the MP: one of the best networking rooms of the year for government relations. Tickets through the Chamber.
gr_note: The Chamber is the region's main business advocacy voice; this is the year's best room to meet its board, members and the politicians they lobby.
organizer: Kelowna Chamber of Commerce; co-presented by Lawson Lundell LLP and BEEM Credit Union
attendees: Kelowna business community and Chamber members; local elected officials usually attend

title: 10th Annual Festival of Trees opens (BC Children's Hospital Foundation)
location: Mission Hill Family Estate, 1730 Mission Hill Road, West Kelowna, BC
desc: Decorated trees from local business sponsors go on display Nov 20, 2026 to Jan 3, 2027 at Mission Hill in Dan Albas's riding; public tasting experiences run Nov 21 to Dec 31 ($65, $35 members), with part of the proceeds going to BC Children's Hospital Foundation. The sponsor tree-trimming party (Nov 19, 5:30–7:30 p.m.) is for sponsors only.

title: Parade with a Purpose 2026 (KGH Foundation)
location: Downtown Kelowna, BC (exact venue TBC; KGH Foundation office: 2268 Pandosy Street, Kelowna)
desc: KGH Foundation fundraiser supporting Kelowna General Hospital, listed for the evening of Dec 5 downtown. The exact venue and format weren't published on the Foundation's calendar; check the event page. Hospital foundation events typically draw local business leaders and elected officials.
gr_note: Hospital foundation events draw health-care leaders and donors; health care is a top provincial issue in the region.
unconfirmed: Exact venue, format and ticketing not yet published.

title: Kelowna Council: 2027 Budget Deliberations
location: Council Chamber, Kelowna City Hall, 1435 Water Street, Kelowna, BC
desc: The new council's first budget: a full-day session where council works through the draft 2027 financial plan line by line and sets the property tax increase. The draft budget is expected to be posted online around Nov. 25. The public can attend in person or watch the livestream.
gr_note: The first real test of the new council's spending priorities (public safety, infrastructure, housing). Read the draft budget before Dec. 3 and watch which departments and capital projects councillors push back on.
attendees: Mayor and council, City Manager, finance and department heads, media
access: Open to the public (no public input during deliberations)
agenda: Draft 2027 budget expected at kelowna.ca around Nov. 25
unconfirmed: Date and 9 a.m. start come from a local newsletter; venue (Council Chamber) and end time assumed. Confirm at kelowna.ca/council.
